summary: Yahweh says to my Lord, sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool. Yahweh will send forth rod of strength out of Zion, rule in midst of enemies, your people offer themselves willingly in day of power in holy array, from womb of dawn. Yahweh has sworn and will not relent, you are priest forever after order of Melchizedek. Lord at your right hand will crush kings in day of wrath, judge among nations, drink from brook by the way therefore lifts head.
whyItMatters: Most quoted Old Testament chapter in New Testament — Jesus uses to stump Pharisees, Peter at Pentecost, Hebrews for priest after Melchizedek, not Levi. Two oracles: king at right hand and priest forever.

context.author: By attribution to David; a court psalm whose date is debated

keyVerses.text: A Psalm by David. Yahweh says to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool for your feet.”
keyVerses.why: Yahweh to my Lord sit at right hand until enemies footstool — most cited.

keyVerses.text: Yahweh has sworn, and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
keyVerses.why: Oath — priest forever not Aaron but Melchizedek order.

themes: sit at right hand until enemies footstool

questions.question: Why does David say 'Yahweh says to my Lord sit at my right hand'? Who is my Lord if David is king?
questions.answer: In its original setting, most scholars read this as a royal-court psalm — an enthronement oracle for a reigning king of David's line, with 'my lord' the king. Jewish tradition has generally read it that way, non-messianically. Jesus invokes it in Matthew 22:41-45 as a riddle: if the Messiah is David's son, why does David call him Lord? The church reads the psalm's king as greater than David — a reading the New Testament claims and the original court setting does not, by itself, prove. Both readings agree the psalm puts a king at God's right hand; they disagree about which king.

questions.question: What does 'priest forever after order of Melchizedek' mean?
questions.answer: Israelite priests are Levites after Aaron order. Melchizedek in Genesis 14 is king of Salem (Jerusalem) and priest of God Most High who blesses Abraham, brings bread wine, and Abraham gives tithe. No genealogy listed, appears then disappears — ideal for priest forever, not based on lineage. Psalm says Messiah will be priest not after Levi but after Melchizedek — king-priest combo, superior, oath not changeable. Hebrews 7 explains: Melchizedek greater than Abraham, therefore Jesus' priesthood greater than Levitical.

questions.question: Why does it say 'from womb of dawn youth like dew' and 'drink from brook by way lifts head'? Obscure.
questions.answer: Verse 3 Hebrew difficult: 'from womb of dawn your youth is to you like dew' — image of people offering willingly in holy garments, youthful vigor renewed like dew at dawn. Dew = fresh, innumerable. Verse 7: he will drink from brook by the way therefore lifts head — warrior king pauses to drink on march, refreshed, lifts head in victory. Some read as Messiah refreshed on path to crushing kings. Both verses use obscure poetry for vitality.

glossary.def: Place of honor, co-rule, until enemies made footstool.
Genesis 14:18-20 king of Salem and priest of God Most High, no genealogy, type of eternal priest.
Enemies subdued under feet — ancient victory image of total defeat.
